payload.task_text:
Our company is launching a wellness program and I have been asked to coordinate the cafeteria lunch menu for the upcoming week. There is a corporate nutrition guidelines page available at http://localhost:30206/guidelines.html that outlines the daily nutritional intake targets for a healthy adult, including recommended calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrate amounts per meal, along with notes about common dietary restrictions our employees have reported such as vegetarian and low-sodium preferences.

Please start by visiting that guidelines page and extracting all the nutritional targets and dietary notes listed there. The page has a table with per-meal targets for lunch specifically, and a section listing the top dietary restrictions reported by employees.

Next, search the recipe database for Chinese dishes that would be suitable for a corporate cafeteria lunch. I need you to find at least two main dishes from the meat category, at least two dishes from the vegetable category, and at least one soup or staple dish. For each dish, note the name, category, and any available ingredient or preparation details.

Once you have the recipes, create a Google Sheets spreadsheet called "Wellness_Lunch_Menu" with a sheet named "Weekly_Plan". This sheet should have columns for Day (Monday through Friday), Main_Dish_1, Main_Dish_2, Side_Dish, Soup_Or_Staple, Estimated_Calories, Estimated_Protein_g, Estimated_Fat_g, and Estimated_Carbs_g. Assign the recipes you found across the five days, reusing dishes if needed but trying to vary the menu. Fill in estimated nutritional values per meal based on reasonable estimates for Chinese dishes, keeping them within the guidelines you found on the website. Add a second sheet called "Nutrition_Summary" with columns for Nutrient, Daily_Target, Menu_Average, and Within_Target (Yes or No), with rows for Calories, Protein, Fat, and Carbs.

After the spreadsheet is ready, write a Word document called Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx in the workspace. This document should have a title "Corporate Wellness Lunch Program", a brief introduction explaining the program goals, a section listing the five daily menus with dish names, and a section summarizing how the menu aligns with the nutritional guidelines. Mention any dishes that accommodate dietary restrictions.

Finally, send an email from wellness@company.com to cafeteria-manager@company.com with the subject "Weekly Wellness Lunch Menu - March 2026" that provides an overview of the meal plan, highlights the nutritional targets from the guidelines, and lists all the dishes selected for the week.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, run the four independent read-only sources in one wave and keep their complete page/category responses out of the main context. The recipe categories can exceed the model-output limit, so their owners must be explore sub-agents constrained to read-only source work; they may read the runtime `output_path` but must not write a deliverable or mutate any external system.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 4 explore sub-agents as parallel individual Agent calls:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to read the complete nutrition-guidelines page at `http://localhost:30206/guidelines.html` with read-only browser operations. Return the exact lunch targets for calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrates, every reported dietary restriction/note, and page/table/field controls.
   2. explore 1 (web-domain-researcher 1): Use one strictly read-only explore sub-agent to query exact recipe category `荤菜`. If the response is materialized as an overlong runtime `output_path`, read that file from the task workspace instead of retrying the category call. Select at least two distinct cafeteria-suitable recipe IDs, retrieve only those exact IDs in native parallel, and return `{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], category:"荤菜", category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}`. Do not write a deliverable or modify a recipe.
   3. explore 2 (web-domain-researcher 2): Use one strictly read-only explore sub-agent to query exact recipe category `素菜`. If the response is materialized as an overlong runtime `output_path`, read that file from the task workspace instead of retrying the category call. Select at least two distinct cafeteria-suitable recipe IDs, retrieve only those exact IDs in native parallel, and return `{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], category:"素菜", category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}`. Do not write a deliverable or modify a recipe.
   4. explore 3 (web-domain-researcher 3): Use one strictly read-only explore sub-agent to query exact category `汤`; only when that returned collection has no usable recipe may it query exact category `主食`. Consume any overlong runtime `output_path` from the task workspace without repeating the call, select at least one suitable exact recipe ID, retrieve only that ID, and return `{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], requested_category:"汤", used_category, fallback_reason, category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}`. Do not write a deliverable or modify a recipe.

After Wave 1, the main agent must require at least two meat, two vegetable, and one soup/staple recipe with unique exact IDs, freeze an explicit Monday-Friday menu (reusing only those verified dishes when needed), and derive reasonable meal-level estimates that remain consistent with the source targets. Freeze the task-visible agent-workspace absolute path from the Visible Boundary/current working directory; never assume `/workspace`. From that frozen menu, dispatch the three independent output branches in the same response: (1) coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): own exactly one `Wellness_Lunch_Menu` spreadsheet with `Weekly_Plan` and `Nutrition_Summary` using the task's exact columns/rows; (2) coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): own `<agent_workspace>/Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx` with the exact title, five daily menus, guideline alignment, and supported dietary accommodations; and (3) coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): send exactly one message from `wellness@company.com` to `cafeteria-manager@company.com` with subject `Weekly Wellness Lunch Menu - March 2026`. Read both artifacts once in native-parallel calls, then reconcile dish names, targets, estimates, averages, Within_Target decisions, and email content. Do not dispatch a verification agent.

nodes.text:
You have access to the howtocook MCP recipe database tools (mcp__howtocook__*). Your job is read-only research: fetch recipe details and return a compact digest.

Use the tool `mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById` with the `query` parameter set to each dish name below (fuzzy matching on Chinese names works). For each dish, extract: the recipe id, category (from the id pattern, e.g. meat_dish / vegetable_dish / soup / staple), a short list of key ingredients (5-10 items, skip equipment/tools), estimated cooking difficulty (the star rating), and a one-sentence preparation summary from the description or steps.

Dishes to look up (query with the Chinese name only, without 的做法):
1. 宫保鸡丁
2. 孜然牛肉
3. 黄焖鸡
4. 鱼香肉丝
5. 凉拌鸡丝
6. 西红柿炒鸡蛋
7. 地三鲜
8. 鸡蛋羹
9. 松仁玉米
10. 凉拌豆腐
11. 蒜蓉西兰花
12. 白灼菜心
13. 酸辣土豆丝
14. 素炒豆角
15. 炒青菜
16. 西红柿鸡蛋汤
17. 紫菜蛋花汤
18. 金针菇汤
19. 电饭煲蒸米饭 (if not found, try 蒸米饭 or 煮锅蒸米饭)
20. 蛋炒饭

If a dish is not found under one name, try the alternative name given. Do not give up after one attempt.

Return your findings as a single structured report in this exact format per dish:

### <Name>
- ID: <id>
- Category: <meat_dish|vegetable_dish|soup|staple>
- Key ingredients: <comma-separated short list>
- Difficulty: <stars>
- Preparation: <one sentence>
- Vegetarian: Yes/No (based on ingredients: any meat/fish/pork = No; egg/tofu/vegetables only = Yes)
- Contains pork: Yes/No
- Notes: anything relevant for a low-sodium or gluten-free diet (e.g. heavy soy sauce use), otherwise "none"

Be concise. Do not paste full recipes.
Fetch recipe details digest

Build the content of an existing Word document using the mcp__word__* tools. The file already exists (created empty) at:
FILENAME = /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-playwright-howtocook-nutrition-gsheet-email/workspace/Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx

IMPORTANT: All mcp__word__ add_* calls append to the end of the document. Issue them ONE AT A TIME, strictly sequentially (each call reads/saves the file; parallel calls on the same file will conflict and lose content). Use FILENAME (absolute path) in every call.

Build the document in EXACTLY this order:

1. add_heading (level 1, bold): Corporate Wellness Lunch Program
2. add_paragraph: This document summarizes the cafeteria lunch menu for the Corporate Wellness Program week of Monday, March 10 through Friday, March 14, 2026. Developed by the wellness committee in partnership with registered dietitians, the program aims to provide balanced Chinese-cuisine lunches that support employee health while respecting the dietary needs of our diverse workforce. The complete day-by-day plan with nutritional estimates is maintained in the Google Sheets workbook \u201cWellness_Lunch_Menu\u201d (sheets: Weekly_Plan and Nutrition_Summary).
3. add_heading (level 2): Program Goals and Nutritional Guidelines
4. add_paragraph: Per the Corporate Wellness Nutrition Guidelines 2026, every lunch tray must fall within the following per-serving targets: 500\u2013800 kcal (target 650), 20\u201345 g protein (target 30 g), 15\u201330 g fat (target 22 g), and 55\u2013110 g carbohydrates (target 80 g). Each meal must include at least one protein-rich main dish (15 g+ protein), at least one vegetable dish, and one soup or rice/noodle staple. No dish may be repeated excessively across the five days, and a fully vegetarian main dish must be offered daily.
5. add_heading (level 2): Weekly Lunch Menu (March 10\u201314, 2026)
6. addparagraph-style note — use add_paragraph with: All dishes were sourced from the approved Chinese recipe database. Categories: meat dishes, vegetable dishes, soups, and staples. Each day pairs one meat main with one vegetarian main, one vegetable side, and a soup or staple.
7. add_table with rows=6, cols=5 and this data (row by row):
["Day", "Main Dish 1", "Main Dish 2 (Vegetarian)", "Side Dish", "Soup or Staple"],
["Monday March 10", "Kung Pao Chicken (gong bao ji ding)", "Tomato Egg Stir-fry (xi hong shi chao ji dan)", "Hot & Sour Shredded Potato (suan la tu dou si)", "Steamed Rice (staple)"],
["Tuesday March 11", "Cumin Beef (zi ran niu rou)", "Di San Xian - potato, eggplant & pepper (di san xian)", "Saut\u00e9ed Green Vegetables (chao qing cai)", "Tomato Egg Drop Soup (soup)"],
["Wednesday March 12", "Braised Chicken with Mushrooms (huang men ji)", "Steamed Egg Custard (ji dan geng)", "Blistered Green Peppers (hu pi qing jiao)", "Scallion Oil Noodles (staple)"],
["Thursday March 13", "Yu-Shiang Shredded Pork - CONTAINS PORK (yu xiang rou si)", "Corn with Pine Nuts (song ren yu mi)", "Wood Ear Mushroom Salad (liang ban mu er)", "Seaweed Egg Drop Soup (soup)"],
["Friday March 14", "Cold Shredded Chicken (liang ban ji si)", "Cold Tofu (liang ban dou fu)", "Smashed Cucumber Salad (liang ban huang gua)", "Enoki Mushroom Soup (soup)"]
8. After the table, call format_table on table_index 0 with has_header_row=true, then highlight_table_header on table_index 0 (header_color "2C5530").
9. add_heading (level 2): Alignment with the Nutritional Guidelines
10. add_paragraph: The menu was planned so that every day falls within the guideline ranges, and the five-day averages land close to the dietitians' targets: 646 kcal vs. the 650 kcal target, 31.8 g protein vs. 30 g, 21.8 g fat vs. 22 g, and 76.4 g carbohydrates vs. 80 g. Composition requirements are met daily: every tray includes a 15 g+ protein main, a vegetable side, and a soup or staple; soups are light broth-based preparations; and all 20 menu slots use distinct dishes (zero repeats, comfortably within the no-more-than-2-repeating-dishes rule).
11. add_table with rows=5, cols=6 and this data:
["Nutrient", "Minimum", "Target", "Maximum", "Menu Average", "Within Target"],
["Calories (kcal)", "500", "650", "800", "646", "Yes"],
["Protein (g)", "20", "30", "45", "31.8", "Yes"],
["Fat (g)", "15", "22", "30", "21.8", "Yes"],
["Carbohydrates (g)", "55", "80", "110", "76.4", "Yes"]
12. format_table on table_index 1 with has_header_row=true, then highlight_table_header on table_index 1 (header_color "2C5530").
13. add_heading (level 2): Dietary Restriction Accommodations
14. add_paragraph (bold=true): Vegetarian (23% of employees): every day provides a fully vegetarian main dish \u2014 Tomato Egg Stir-fry (Mon), Di San Xian (Tue), Steamed Egg Custard (Wed), Corn with Pine Nuts (Thu), and Cold Tofu (Fri). All soups served are also meat-free.
15. add_paragraph (bold=true): Low-Sodium (18%): the kitchen is instructed to reduce soy sauce and salt in the higher-sodium recipes (Kung Pao Chicken, Braised Chicken, Yu-Shiang Shredded Pork) and to favor low-sodium options such as Cold Shredded Chicken, Corn with Pine Nuts, Seaweed Egg Drop Soup, and Smashed Cucumber Salad.
16. add_paragraph (bold=true): Gluten-Free (12%): naturally gluten-free options are available every day \u2014 steamed rice, tofu, egg custard, corn, potato dishes, and broth-based soups; gluten-free soy sauce is available on request. Note that noodle dishes and soy-sauce-based sauces contain wheat.
17. add_paragraph (bold=true): No Pork (15%): only one dish this week contains pork \u2014 Yu-Shiang Shredded Pork on Thursday \u2014 and it is clearly labeled on the serving line. All other dishes are pork-free.
18. add_heading (level 2): Notes for the Cafeteria Team
19. add_paragraph: Estimated per-tray nutrition: Monday 680 kcal / 34 g protein / 24 g fat / 78 g carbs; Tuesday 640 kcal / 31 g / 22 g / 76 g; Wednesday 700 kcal / 36 g / 24 g / 82 g; Thursday 650 kcal / 30 g / 22 g / 80 g; Friday 560 kcal / 28 g / 17 g / 66 g. Please label all dishes with names and allergen/pork indicators, and portion each component as a single serving so the estimates remain accurate.

After building, verify by calling get_document_outline and get_document_text on FILENAME; confirm the title, 5 headings, and both tables are present, then report back the outline and any issues.
Build Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx
